name: Eothoracosaurus
isnote: A "thoracosaur", described as a gavialoid (Brochu 2004) but recovered outside crown Crocodylia by tip-dating (Lee & Yates 2018).
sum: Long-snouted Late Cretaceous eusuchian from the Ripley Formation of Mississippi, a close relative of Thoracosaurus.
holotype: MSU 3293 — skull and associated postcranial bones, Dunn-Seiler Museum, Mississippi.
material: The holotype, first referred to Thoracosaurus neocesariensis.
biology: The sources say nothing about its biology.
author: Brochu 2004

sources.text: Brochu, Christopher A. 2004. A new Late Cretaceous gavialoid crocodylian from eastern North America and the phylogenetic relationships of thoracosaurs. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 24(3): 610–633. doi:10.1671/0272-4634(2004)024[0610:ANLCGC]2.0.CO;2
